summary: ACCEPT. Repairs the scanner-capture alert after it produced a FALSE ALARM caused by the S0 credential rotation. ROOT CAUSE: the alert script held the PRE-ROTATION credential; psql authentication failed, stderr was discarded, the return code was ignored, and the script CONVERTED THE FAILURE INTO ROWS=0 -- then asserted a cause it never measured, 'Capture not writing'. Capture was in fact writing: 37 rows across 12 symbols with the newest at 08:55:14 ET, five minutes before the page. THE ALERT WAS WRONG ON THE FACT AND WRONG ON THE CAUSE. ⭐ AND IT WAS ALSO TESTING THE WRONG THING: a `== 0` threshold cannot distinguish 37 from 15,000, so it would have stayed silent at either. The replacement compares against five matching weekdays at the same ET cutoff, alerts below 20% of that median, and prints BOTH populations on every measured line. Production read-only replay: 37 current / 28 baseline = 132.1%, OBSERVED. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION ACROSS TWO ROUNDS. Round 1, baseline 12: M2 (LOW_VOLUME_RATIO 0.20 -> 0.10) DIED, killed by test_low_volume_control_flips_on_only_the_measured_ratio; M4 (flip `ratio <` to `ratio >`) DIED with 3 failures; M3 (remove baseline_median from the emitted line) DIED, so the both-populations requirement is defended. ⛔ M1b SURVIVED with 12 passed: deleting the NONZERO-RETURN-CODE raise left every test green. That gap mattered more than the others because IT IS EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENED DURING S0 -- psql with a dead password EXITS NON-ZERO and writes to stderr, it does not raise a Python exception. The existing test raised RuntimeError('authentication failed'), which covers the EXCEPTION path; the RETURN-CODE path is a different branch and nothing exercised it. The one shape that actually occurred was untested. Round 2, baseline 13, source BYTE-IDENTICAL (0 non-test files changed, 49 test lines added): M1b replay DIED, killed by test_psql_return_code_separates_measured_rows_from_unmeasured_failure. ⭐ M5, which I invented AFTER the correction so it cannot have been written to -- keep the raise but render row_count as 0 instead of UNMEASURED -- DIED with TWO failures including test_unreadable_database_never_becomes_a_measured_zero. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 23dedc2f0991ef52. ⭐ CODEX'S CONTROLLED PAIR IS BETTER THAN WHAT I ASKED FOR: it uses real CompletedProcess objects with rc=2, populated stderr, and DELIBERATELY VALID-LOOKING ZERO STDOUT -- so it tests the dangerous case where the output would parse cleanly. Asserting that rc!=0 never renders rows=0 and never emits LOW_VOLUME is the exact negative that the original defect needed. ⛔ TWO OF MY OWN MUTANTS THIS ROUND WERE INVALID AND I DISCARDED THEM RATHER THAN REPORTING THEM: a first M1 attempt targeted the ValueError parse branch using the WRONG CLASS NAME (Observation vs DatabaseObservation), making it both invalid and unreachable; and an M2 regex failed to match the LOW_VOLUME_RATIO constant so that run produced no result at all. A surviving mutant is often a bad mutant -- only survivors that can be shown valid AND reachable are findings. ⛔ AND A LARGER ERROR OF MINE THIS SESSION, recorded because it nearly cost a wasted escalation: from this defect I inferred that unowned_position_cron.sh was ALSO broken by S0 and escalated it as live-money blindness. It was NOT. Codex refuted it with evidence I then verified myself: the real cron target reads the managed env file and DERIVES PGPASSWORD from it (lines 82-84), 0 checker failures, and an isolated DB-failure control proving it fails LOUD (rc=1, CHECKER-FAILED=1, green verdicts 0). My regex matched the STRING 'PGPASSWORD=' without distinguishing EMBEDDED from DERIVED, and I escalated WITHOUT OPENING THE FILE -- the path I named does not even exist. A pattern match is a lead, not a finding. ADOPTED RULE, codex's wording, to be enforced in CI: production scripts load the DSN from the managed env, validate exactly one value and a real connection, and convert every DB failure to COULD_NOT_TELL/UNMEASURED with a NONZERO EXIT, never zero; CI scans RESOLVED CRON TARGETS, not filename patterns. NOT MEASURED: I ran the focused test file only -- codex reports 2,968 passed with 14 skipped, taken on report. I did not exercise the installer's copy/backup/readback/rollback myself; that is accepted on their report. ⛔ DEPLOY: ops-only, needs a full checkout sync plus install_scanner_capture_verify.sh. No service restart. It is read-only by construction and touches no capture-writer code.
